reason: Mechanical tripwire for macOS idle/occluded CPU recurrence (Perf §alarming-3). The 128–195% idle-CPU class has recurred twice (caught only socially); this gate asserts the backdrop/animation pause guard behavior so a future regression cannot merge silently.

gate.scope: macOS backdrop WebGL render-loop occlusion pause (KernelBackdropView → window.__setBackdropActive → setHostVisible → cancelAnimationFrame)
assertions: JS bundle __setBackdropActive(false) cancels pending requestAnimationFrame and stops scheduling while hidden
JS bundle __setBackdropActive(true) resumes the rAF loop (new rAF scheduled)
JS bundle with cancelAnimationFrame gutted is caught (rAF not cancelled on occlusion)
Swift OcclusionVisibilityPolicy returns inactive for no-window and occluded states, active for visible

measurementLimitations.reason: GitHub Actions macOS runners do not support real NSWindow occlusion state transitions; a headless app launch cannot exercise the occlusion→rAF-cancel path at runtime. The behavioral tripwire (exercising the real JS bundle in a mock DOM+rAF harness) is the strongest executable gate available in CI.
measurementLimitations.localVerification: On a real Mac, launch the app, occlude the window, and confirm Activity Monitor shows ~0% CPU (documented in PetCompanion BUILD-NOTES.md §Idle CPU).

seededValues.note: This is a NEW budget for a NEW gate; no existing baseline was raised.

trendPolicy.name: occlusion-pause-behavioral-ratchet
trendPolicy.rule: The behavioral tripwire must pass on every PR. If the occlusion guard is removed or weakened, the tripwire fails. The tripwire may only be relaxed with A5 (Alberto) sign-off and a written rationale in the PR body.
